cues.text: Everything here was built during the hackathon. The doors and the hallway are from a real home; the other scenes are simulated, and labelled.
This bathroom threshold is three and a half centimetres. For someone with a walker, who notices?
SafePath: film the home, get it measured, get the paperwork, and prove the fix.
Phone video goes to SAM 3.1, then a rule table, then a Muse Spark agent, then a draft subsidy package, then a re-shoot.

Real doors. SAM 3.1 finds the door, and an A4 sheet gives the scale. The front door reads 84.9 centimetres; the tape says 90. Our error is about ten percent, so a width is only a reference, plus or minus ten percent. The bathroom door runs off the photo, so the app reports no width at all.
The bathroom threshold reads 3.8 centimetres, next to the 3 centimetre line. When our error is as big as the margin, SafePath does not decide. It asks for a tape measure. The tape says 3.5.
Real hallway, one walk-through video. SAM 3.1 tracks each object across the frames. A cable and two slippers lie on the walking path, so they are red. Bags against the wall are only noted.
Verdicts come from a rule table, not from the model, so every number can be traced to a code article.
The agent looks at the photo of every finding before trusting it. SAM 3.1 scored this sticker 0.9 as shoes. The agent handed it to a person.

When a tool refuses a value, the agent corrects itself. In the real hallway, it wrote the word null as a subsidy code three times, was refused each time, and sent the work orders without one. It cannot change a number.
The family gets a clearing list for today, and work orders. Clutter needs no subsidy.
Construction items do. For a threshold ramp, SafePath drafts a Taiwan long-term-care subsidy package with official item codes and caps. It stays a draft until a care professional reviews it.
After the fix, the same route is filmed again. The cable and both slippers are gone. Three of three items, verified fixed: red to green.
Construction fixes must be seen. Muse Spark compares before and after, so a missed detection can't pass as a repair. This home is simulated.
SAM 3.1 sees and measures. Muse Spark does the paperwork. The code is public. See it. Fix it. Prove it.
